# Didache Chapter 11 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Hierosolymitanus (H), Didache 11 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/DID_011_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 11

**1** Receive anyone who comes and teaches you all the things said above.

**2** But if a teacher turns aside and teaches a different doctrine that undermines what was stated above, do not listen to him. However, if his teaching promotes greater righteousness and knowledge of the Lord, receive him as you would the Lord.

**3** Concerning apostles and prophets: follow the rule of the Gospel.

**4** Welcome every apostle who comes to you as you would welcome the Lord.

**5** But he is not to stay more than one day; if necessary, two days. If he stays three days, he is a false prophet.

**6** When the apostle leaves, he is to take only enough bread to last until his next destination. If he asks for money, he is a false prophet.

**7** Do not test or pass judgment on any prophet who speaks in the Spirit — for every sin shall be forgiven, but this sin shall not be forgiven.

**8** Not everyone who speaks in the Spirit is a prophet — only the one whose conduct is in keeping with the Lord. By their conduct, the false prophet and the true prophet are to be distinguished.

**9** Any prophet who in the Spirit commands a meal to be set — shall not eat from it himself; if he does eat from it, he is a false prophet.

**10** Every prophet who teaches the truth — if he does not practice what he teaches, he is a false prophet.

**11** But as for a proven prophet who enacts the worldly mystery of the Church — do not judge him, provided he does not teach others to do the same. His judgment belongs to God, for the ancient prophets acted in this way as well.

**12** If anyone says in the Spirit, "Give me money" — or anything else — do not listen to him. But if he directs that gifts be given to others who are in need, no one is to judge him.

---

*LOGOS notes: Ch. 11 reflects a community navigating the challenge of itinerant charismatic ministry. The tests provided are practical: duration of stay (v.5), financial requests (v.6, v.12), conduct (v.8), consistency between teaching and practice (v.10). V.7's prohibition of testing prophets "in the Spirit" echoes the Blasphemy against the Holy Spirit (Matt 12:31). V.11's "worldly mystery of the Church" (μυστήριον κοσμικὸν ἐκκλησίας) is notoriously obscure — most interpreters think it refers to a prophetic symbolic action (like Hosea's marriage) that represents spiritual realities.*
